properties.name: The hosted surface can refuse every write, enforced at the one point a write cannot avoid
properties.rationale:
WHY THE WRITE GUARD AND NOT A LIST OF TOOL NAMES. A write cannot happen without taking the guard, so refusing to hand one out is a rule the type system enforces rather than one somebody maintains. The alternative — a list of mutating tools, or a check keyed on `readOnlyHint` — is a rule maintained by hand with nothing checking it, which is the exact defect class this project fixed three times on 2026-08-26 (`unallocated_component` and the parking ruling, F-01's replay contract, and three detectors not reading `proposed`). Choosing the hand-maintained form here, on the same day, would have been remarkable.

⭐ THE COMPILER PROVED THE SWEEP COMPLETE, which is the property the factory brainstorm was reaching for. Making `write_lock` fallible turned all 98 call sites into compile errors until each was updated — no list, no audit, no chance of missing one.

⭐ AND IT FOUND A CASE REVIEW WOULD NOT HAVE. `share()` is a SECOND assembly point, minting a service per CLIENT SESSION for `req:sessions-share-a-graph`. Read-only had to be INHERITED there. Had it been reset, the mode would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client — and a client session is the only way anybody reaches a shared server, so the feature would have been read-only in name only while testing green at the process level. Pinned by `a_session_on_a_read_only_server_is_read_only_too`.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DELIVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. INTEGRITY is answered outright: no write means nothing to attribute, so the caller-supplied `contributor_id` — an unverified claim over a network — is never accepted. CONFIDENTIALITY is NOT eliminated, only RELOCATED to the network, which is what binding to a tailnet is for. The requirement says this in its own words and it must not be read as authentication being unnecessary, only as it not blocking the first cut.

⚠️ AND IT CHANGES NOTHING FOR AN ORDINARY SESSION, verified rather than asserted. `a_normal_service_still_writes` asserts a default service is writable and passed BEFORE the refusal existed and after it. Every shipped config launches without the flag. This change event was itself written through a shared server running the new binary, which is the same demonstration a user would want.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `--read-only` added to reflow2-mcp, delivering `req:the-hosted-surface-is-read-only-so-it-can-ship-before-authentication-exists`. Enforced in `ReflowService::write_lock`, which every mutating handler must call to obtain the graph's write guard — so it covers all 98 existing write sites and every write added later, including by an author who never heard of the mode. OFF BY DEFAULT: `read_only: false` in `wrap_at`, the single assembly point, and the flag is absent from every shipped config. Four pins in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/a_read_only_surface_refuses_every_write.rs. Workspace suite 1817 passed / 0 failed across 159 binaries; fmt and clippy clean.
